lots.title: Multi-disciplinary Design Team Appointment — Stockport Town Centre School (Architect scope, Annex A.1)
lots.description: Appointment of an architecturally led multi-disciplinary design team to develop a feasibility-through-to-concept design of a new school in a town-centre location. This document (Annex A.1) defines the Architect's scope of service within the multi-disciplinary appointment, covering Lead Consultant / Design Team Leader duties, BIM compliance, Risk Register contribution, and full RIBA Plan of Work 2020 Stage 0–7 responsibilities. The appointment is under a JCT Design & Build Contract with consultant novation, with payment on 30-day terms on stage completion. The Architect is responsible for coordinating all design outputs across roofing, waterproofing, flooring, ceilings, walling, doors/ironmongery, screens, architectural metalwork, finishes, FF&E, shading, façade and cladding (including glazed balustrades), toilets, BMS spatial allowances, wayfinding/signage, feature structural expressions, and an access and maintenance strategy.
requirements: Architect acts as Lead Consultant and Design Team Leader (Core Services 1.2).
Comply with Client Organisational Information Requirements for BIM and Employer's Information Requirements for BIM; run clash detection reviews and minimisation meetings (Core Services 1.3).
Chair and minute design/project/construction meetings and distribute records across design and construction teams (Core Services 1.4).

Supply fully coordinated design covering architectural scope 1.6.1–1.6.18 including roofing, waterproofing, flooring, ceilings, walling, doors & ironmongery, acoustic/privacy screens, architectural metalwork, decorations & finishes, FF&E, shading systems, façade and cladding with glazed balustrades, toilets, BMS spatial requirements, statutory and wayfinding signage, architectural intent for expressed structural features, and access & maintenance strategy.
Contribute to and maintain the Project Risk Register; issue Designers Risk Assessments at the end of each stage (Core Services 1.8–1.9).
Support the BREEAM assessor to ensure the target BREEAM rating is met (Core Services 1.11).
Design the works to comply with all relevant statutory requirements, codes of practice, guidance and best practice; raise derogation notices where compliance is not met (Core Services 1.16–1.18).
Manage the gaining of Planning Permissions and Building Control Applications (Core Services 1.19).
Ensure proposals comply with the Disability Discrimination Act (Core Services 1.20).
Make drawings available in both PDF and DWG format; maintain a Common Data Environment (Core Services 1.21, 1.23).
Issue a monthly Design Progress report and maintain a design programme, also issued monthly (Core Services 1.22).
Comply with the RIBA Plan of Work 2020 for Stages 0/1, 2, 3, 4, 5 and 6/7, providing a formal stage report at the conclusion of each stage (Sections 2.1–2.2, 3.1–3.2, 4.1–4.2, 5.1–5.2, 6.1, 7.1).

At RIBA Stage 2 produce site plan, general arrangement drawings (plans, elevations, sections with dimensions/datums/levels), roof plans, larger-scale details for complex areas, and area/accommodation schedules (Section 3.4).

At RIBA Stage 3 produce grid drawings, 1:100 & 1:50 GAs, fully coordinated full site plan, external elevations with detailed bay studies, 1:100 roof layout, 1:50 stair/ramp sections proving rise/going/pitch, coordinated ceiling layouts with void depth zones, room data sheets, and area/accommodation schedules (Section 4.4).

At RIBA Stages 3–4 prepare calculations, drawings, schedules and specifications to enable tender documentation; coordinate submissions to statutory authorities; undertake value management and support cost planning (Sections 4.5–4.17, 5.3–5.11).
At RIBA Stage 5 issue Construction-status drawings, schedules, calculations and specifications; attend site meetings; record defects and handover plan (Section 6.2–6.6).
At RIBA Stages 6–7 manage snagging, defects administration, post-completion services, O&M input, Health & Safety File contributions and Lessons Learnt workshops (Sections 7.1–7.7).
Comply with the CDM Regulations and update the pre-construction information and Health and Safety File throughout (Sections 2.10, 3.9, 4.6, 4.10, 5.5, 7.5–7.6).
Employer's Liability insurance of £10,000,000 (General 1.6).
Public Liability insurance of £10,000,000 with indemnity-to-principals provision and no aggregate limit on number of claims (General 1.7).

Professional Indemnity Insurance cover of £20,000,000 per claim (General 1.8 — note text says 'ten million pounds' in parentheses despite figure of £20,000,000; treat the £20,000,000 figure as controlling but flag the inconsistency).
Payment terms: 30 days, invoices following completion of stages (General 1.5).
Form of Building Contract: JCT Design & Build (General 1.3).
Form of Consultant Appointment: Multi Discipline consultant with novation (General 1.4).

warnings.message: This document (Annex A.1 Architectural Scope of Service) does not state evaluation criteria, weightings or award methodology. Evaluation criteria are expected to be defined elsewhere in the tender pack (e.g. 1A-Invitation-to-Participate or 2-Specification) and must be merged at the lot level from those documents, not from this annex.

No CPV code appears anywhere in the Architectural Scope of Service document; CPV must be sourced from the notice or from the Invitation-to-Participate document. The notice-level main_category '150000 - Consultancy' is a ProContract/Proactis category and is not a CPV code, so it has not been emitted as a CPV.

This document is one of several discipline scope annexes (A.1 Architect, A.2 BR Principal Designer, A.3 Mechanical & Electrical, A.4 CDM Principal Designer, A.5 Structural and Civils). It describes only the Architect discipline within a single multi-disciplinary Lot 1 appointment — it does not introduce additional lots. Lot numbering has been preserved as Lot 1 consistent with existing notice-level lot metadata.

Section 1.8 of General specifies Professional Indemnity Insurance Cover Required as '£20,000,000 (ten million pounds)' — the figure (£20,000,000) does not match the parenthetical wording ('ten million pounds'). The figure has been treated as controlling but the mismatch should be queried before reliance.

Docling structural output for this document reports page_count=0 and a single structural section labelled 'page header' with an empty table shell. Page references have been emitted as 'p1' consistently because the markdown content is present even though page-level pagination metadata is unavailable.

The document's numbered-list structure restarts at '1. General' and then '1. Core Services' (the second top-level item is re-labelled '1' rather than '2'). Downstream sections use top-level numbers 2–7 for the RIBA stages. Section references have been preserved using the document's labelling (e.g. 'General 1.x', 'Core Services 1.x', '2.x'–'7.x') rather than renumbering.
